I1.quote: The samples were further characterized for their hydrogen storage capacity using Sieverts apparatus (pressure-composition-isotherms) at three temperatures (77 K, 273 K and 298 K) and 20 bar H2 pressure.

I2.quote: At 77 K, the hydrogen storage capacity for rGO, B-rGO and Ni-B-rGO are 9.8 wt.%, 8.2 wt.% and 6.9 wt.% respectively.

I3.quote: The pressure composition isotherm of rGO, B-rGO, Ni-B-rGO samples measured at 77 K, 273 K and 298 K at 20 bar pressure are shown in Fig. 8.

I4.quote: The reason for such higher storage can be rationalized by the higher specific surface area (897 m2/g) of rGO when compared to other samples
I4.location: main, p. 6, Results and discussion (values in si1, p. 3, Table S2)

I5.quote: Graphene oxide (GO) based derivatives have been explored for hydrogen storage application, owing to their high surface area, low density and tunable pore size.
